import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
try:
    df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("Dataset not found. Please ensure 'data/dogs_zurich.csv' is in the correct directory.")
    exit()

# --- Data Preparation ---

# Clean up the primary breed names for consistency
df['Rasse1Text'] = df['Rasse1Text'].str.strip().str.title()

# Determine the most recent year in the dataset to identify currently popular breeds
latest_year = df['StichtagDatJahr'].max()

# Find the top 10 most common breeds in the most recent year
top_10_breeds = df[df['StichtagDatJahr'] == latest_year]['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().nlargest(10).index

# Filter the dataset to include only the top 10 breeds over all available years
df_top_breeds = df[df['Rasse1Text'].isin(top_10_breeds)]

# Group by year and breed to count registrations
breed_trends = df_top_breeds.groupby(['StichtagDatJahr', 'Rasse1Text']).size().reset_index(name='count')

# --- Visualization ---

# Set a professional plot style and create the figure
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 9))

# Create the line plot showing trends over time
sns.lineplot(
    data=breed_trends,
    x='StichtagDatJahr',
    y='count',
    hue='Rasse1Text',
    style='Rasse1Text',
    markers=True,
    dashes=False,
    linewidth=2.5,
    palette='viridis',
    ax=ax
)

# --- Formatting and Labeling ---

# Set an informative title and subtitle
fig.suptitle(
    "Popularity Trends of Top 10 Dog Breeds in Zurich",
    fontsize=20,
    fontweight='bold',
    y=1.0
)
ax.set_title(
    f"Annual registration counts for the most popular breeds as of {int(latest_year)}",
    fontsize=12,
    pad=15,
    color='dimgray'
)

# Set clear axis labels
ax.set_xlabel("Year of Registration", fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', labelpad=10)
ax.set_ylabel("Number of Registered Dogs", fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', labelpad=10)

# Customize axis ticks for readability
ax.tick_params(axis='both', which='major', labelsize=11)
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MaxNLocator(integer=True)) # Ensure years are integers
plt.setp(ax.get_xticklabels(), rotation=0)

# Format the y-axis to include commas for thousands
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda x, p: format(int(x), ',')))


# Improve the legend
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
ax.legend(
    handles=handles,
    labels=labels,
    title='Dog Breed',
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.03, 1),
    loc='upper left',
    borderaxespad=0.,
    fontsize=11,
    title_fontsize=13,
    shadow=True,
    frameon=True
)

# Add a subtle grid and remove unnecessary spines
ax.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)
ax.grid(axis='x', linestyle=':', alpha=0.5)
sns.despine(ax=ax, trim=True)

# Adjust layout to make space for the title and legend
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 0.95])

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
